concerns.text: The plan states that five random seeds provide ≈ 0.75 statistical power to detect a medium effect (Cohen’s d ≈ 0.5). This falls short of the conventional 0.80 power threshold, risking a Type II error and undermining the reliability of the paired t‑test comparison.

The adaptive scheduler is justified by a Pearson correlation between prediction entropy and per‑example error (FR‑010). Correlation alone does not establish that manipulating density based on entropy will causally improve performance; difficulty of examples may confound both entropy and error. No experimental control (e.g., randomizing entropy‑based adjustments) is provided to isolate the causal effect of the scheduler.
